This suggests the heavier cost base is being matched by revenue scale for now.

"The current narrative assumes Bankwell Financial Group’s higher ongoing expense base will be fully supported by revenue scale. However, noninterest expense guidance for 2026 has already moved up to a range of $65 million to $67 million from $64 million to $65 million earlier in the year."

This concern shows up clearly in Q3. Reported noninterest expense climbed to US$19.8m once the US$3.0m core conversion hit, and conversion costs of roughly US$0.4m to US$0.5m a quarter are still ahead. Yet guidance keeps underlying noninterest expense at US$65m to US$67m and management lifted both net interest income and fee income outlooks. The quarter validates that the higher cost structure is real. At the same time, the improved margin, record SBA income and a 3.71% NIM currently offset the drag.

The latest figures do not remove that risk.

Q3 tells a mixed story. Margins improved across Propulsion, Engine P&A and Navico, and free cash flow reached US$140m. The concern is that new rails and AI agents erode Mastercard’s role. Q3 data does not yet show that pressure winning out. Cross‑border volume rose 11%, value‑added services grew 19%, and management highlighted early traction in agentic commerce and stablecoin infrastructure through the Global Money Platform and Arc.
